10.1016/j.technovation.2026.103694.a: The disruption of generative artificial intelligence (AI) in creative industries is profound. While AI increasingly acts as a proactive partner in ideation, little is known about how this collaboration relates to professional identity reconstruction and project performance. To examine this, we focus on spatial design (architecture and interior design), where digital generation must translate into strict physical constraints and commercial reality. To understand the human foundations of AI-driven innovation, we conducted a mixed-methods study: 10 qualitative interviews (Gioia methodology) and a survey of 223 spatial design projects from Taiwan and Mainland China. Findings support a mediating role for Professional Identity Reconstruction (PIR) between perceived human-AI collaboration and perceived project performance. Specifically, we uncover a shift from the identity of traditional “craftsmen” to “strategic decision-makers.” Professionals who successfully navigate this reconstruction no longer act as mere manual executors; instead, they exercise strategic judgment over machine-generated outputs. This strategic elevation is associated with an enhanced ability to interpret, constrain, and translate raw AI variations into valuable project outcomes. This paper offers two key contributions. First, it refines the assumption of automatic technological dividends: while direct human-AI collaboration correlates with internal process efficiency, it has an indirect association with external market success through human strategic translation. Second, it advances innovation management literature by conceptualizing PIR as one plausible translating pathway. Our findings suggest that as AI automates execution, the realization of market value shifts toward strategic direction. Ultimately, we advise managers to foster workflows prioritizing human evaluative inputs, ensuring algorithmic capabilities are firmly anchored within professional boundaries and commercial realities.

10.1016/j.technovation.2026.103695.a: The latest research indicates that blockchain technology (BCT) is a powerful tool for organizational risk management, but enterprises often struggle to fully utilize its potential and effectiveness in practical operations. This study explores the configuration of BCT agency mechanism and human agent mechanism in the idiosyncratic risk mitigation that drives success and failure. By leveraging the hybrid agency theory and employing crisp-set Qualitative Comparative Analysis (csQCA) on a sample of Chinese listed firms, we identify distinct pathways to risk mitigation success and failure. The findings of this study reveal that successful risk mitigation is not solely dependent on maximizing technical features or application scope; it often depends on strategically limiting the application scope of the technology to match the organization's governance capabilities. On the contrary, failure typically occurs when enterprises over-expand their technology deployment without the necessary internal expertise or platform dominance to manage this expansion. This study challenges technological determinism and emphasizes the necessity of hierarchical control in blockchain governance. Moreover, by shifting the research focus from structured task allocation to configurational coordination of governance capabilities, we have advanced the hybrid agent theory. This indicates that the feasibility of agent technology depends on whether human capabilities are sufficient to coordinate the scope of the deployed technology.

10.1016/j.technovation.2026.103696.a: Frugal business models have emerged as innovative alternatives for serving low-income markets through affordable, sustainable, and robust solutions, supporting organizational strategies under conditions of resource constraints. Initially developed in the context of emerging economies, these models have increasingly gained relevance in developed countries as well, driven by growing concerns regarding resource efficiency and sustainable consumption. Despite the rising academic interest in frugal innovation, research on frugal business models remains fragmented, with limited consolidation of their defining characteristics, dominant patterns, and broader impacts. To address this gap, this study conducts a systematic literature review using the ProKnow-C method. The analysis of a final portfolio of 74 articles identified 23 illustrative cases of frugal products and services and enabled the mapping of recurring patterns, strategic logics, and challenges associated with frugal business models. The findings indicate that these models can support sustainable innovation strategies; however, further empirical research is required to assess their impacts across both emerging and developed market contexts. Overall, this study contributes to the literature by synthesizing existing knowledge and outlining avenues for future research in this domain.

10.1016/j.technovation.2026.103698.a: Incubators play a vital role in entrepreneurial ecosystems by providing start-ups with resources such as funding, mentorship, and access to networks. Incubator systems differ from traditional organizations because start-ups remain legally and strategically independent, which limits hierarchical control and makes coordination inherently relational. However, existing research tends to emphasize the effects of individual resources, paying less attention to how incubators orchestrate resources through ongoing interaction with ventures, leaving unresolved why incubators with similar resource bases often produce markedly different outcomes. Thus, drawing on Resource Orchestration Theory, this study examines how incubators structure, bundle, and leverage resources, and how orchestration operates across multiple levels to shape start-up growth and incubator performance. Based on a qualitative multi-case study, we identify a four-stage cyclical orchestration process in which incubators (1) structure a foundational resource base, (2) provide tailored initial resource packages, (3) dynamically reconfigure bundled resources as ventures evolve, and (4) activate start-up feedback. Feedback takes concrete forms such as alumni mentoring, network bridging, investment connections, and reputational endorsements, which replenish the incubator's resource base and enable subsequent rounds of support. We further theorize a multi-level mechanism comprising incubator orchestration, start-up orchestration, and joint orchestration; joint orchestration operates through coordinated resource acquisition, bundling, and leveraging, helping explain outcome heterogeneity beyond resource stock differences.

10.1016/j.technovation.2026.103699.a: Venture Studios (VSs) are organizations that create start-ups by acting as founders or co-founders and operating through standardized venture creation processes conducted in parallel. To examine this organizational model and delineate its distinctiveness from others, we developed a global database, conducted multiple case studies with twelve European VSs and two international networks, and administered a worldwide survey. Drawing on human capital and organizational learning perspectives, this study identifies the architectural characteristics and mechanisms through which VSs institutionalize portfolio entrepreneurship. Our findings reveal how VSs convert individual entrepreneurial expertise into organizationally codified human capital. In doing so, VSs extend entrepreneurial agency and cognition from individuals to organizations, offering an organizational model for parallel venture creation. Finally, we clarify how VSs complement other entrepreneurial actors by reducing early-stage uncertainty and generating validated, investment-ready ventures.

10.1016/j.technovation.2026.103700.a: Generative artificial intelligence (GAI) is increasingly used by employees to support creative idea generation, yet less is known about its psychological consequences for employees’ subsequent willingness to remain engaged with those ideas. Drawing on psychological ownership theory, we examine whether GAI usage is associated with lower creative psychological ownership (CPO)—the extent to which employees perceive creative ideas as “theirs”—and, in turn, weaker intentions to elaborate, champion, and implement those ideas. We further propose that this relationship varies across human–GAI collaboration modes, with the negative relationship between GAI usage and CPO being more pronounced under GAI-centric collaboration than under human-centric or symbiotic collaboration. Across two scenario-based experiments (Studies 1–2), two task-based studies involving actual GAI interaction (Studies 3–4), and a multi-wave field study (Study 5), the findings provide converging, although not uniform, evidence for the proposed relationships. A mini meta-analysis further indicates an overall negative association between GAI usage and CPO and positive associations between CPO and downstream innovation-related intentions. Overall, the findings identify a potential psychological cost of GAI-assisted idea generation. They also show how collaboration modes may shape employees’ perceived ownership of ideas and their intentions to continue developing and advancing them.

10.1016/j.technovation.2026.103701.a: As an important manifestation of data-driven technological innovation paradigms, digital transformation has become a key pathway through which multinational enterprises reshape their innovation processes, enhance global competitiveness, and achieve sustainable value creation. It not only transforms firms’ modes of knowledge creation, organizational coordination mechanisms, and resource allocation logic, but also creates new opportunities for multinational enterprises to deepen their global innovation network embedding and improve ESG performance. However, existing studies have rarely systematically explored the impact mechanism of digital transformation on ESG performance from the perspective of global innovation network embedding. Grounded in the resource-based theory and social network theory, using panel data of Chinese A-share listed multinational enterprises from 2010 to 2022, the impact and mechanism of digital transformation on ESG performance in multinational enterprises were empirically analyzed by employing the two-way fixed effects model, the mediation effect model and the moderation effect model. Results indicate that, (1) Digital transformation has a significantly positive effect on the ESG performance. (2) The mechanism through which digital transformation enhances ESG performance lies in accelerating the global innovation network embedding of multinational enterprises. (3) Internal control quality strengthens the positive effect of digital transformation on ESG performance, whereas external environmental uncertainty weakens this effect. (4) The digital transformation has a stronger incentive effect on ESG performance for large-scale, manufacturing, and technology and labor-intensive multinational enterprises. The obtained conclusions contribute to fully leveraging the driving effect of digital transformation by multinational enterprises in the global value chain and provide empirical evidence that such firms can enhance their global collaborative innovation capability and sustainable competitive advantage through digital transformation.

10.1016/j.technovation.2026.103702.a: Strategic R&D management requires foresight tools that are dynamic, uncertainty-aware, and transparent, yet most existing approaches remain static, deterministic, and difficult to interpret. This study introduces PATTERN-X (Patent Analytics Through Temporal Network Evaluation and Reasoning with eXplainability), an explainable AI framework integrating temporal patent network analysis, Bayesian deep learning, and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG). Using 4167 European Patent Office patents in the Intelligent Lighting Systems (ILS) domain (1981–2024), the framework is empirically validated within the European ILS innovation ecosystem. The study addresses three research questions: RQ1 examines how temporal network analysis can reveal the evolution of technology innovation ecosystems; RQ2 investigates how probabilistic deep learning can quantify predictive uncertainty for risk-aware R&D decision-making; and RQ3 explores how generative AI can translate quantitative forecasts into evidence-based strategic narratives. Addressing RQ1, temporal co-classification network analysis reveals ecosystem evolution from 3 to 16 technology clusters and a shift in centrality toward digital control and vehicle-integrated technologies. Addressing RQ2, a Bayesian LSTM achieves an MAE of 0.89, an 88% strategic hit rate, and well-calibrated uncertainty estimates (PICP = 0.91 against a nominal 95% interval, reflecting a slight undercoverage typical of variational approximations), enabling risk-sensitive evaluation of convergence opportunities. Addressing RQ3, a CPC-guided RAG system generates evidence-grounded strategic narratives with high faithfulness (0.85; κ = 0.82), translating probabilistic forecasts into auditable managerial explanations. Together, these results demonstrate how dynamic analysis, uncertainty quantification, and explainable generative AI can enhance technology convergence forecasting and strategic innovation management.

10.1016/j.technovation.2026.103703.a: State-owned enterprises (SOEs) play a pivotal role in national innovation systems, yet their dual mandate of serving public objectives while remaining commercially viable makes it difficult to balance exploratory and exploitative innovation. We examine how administrative rank, a formal position within the party-state hierarchy, shapes this balance in Chinese central SOEs. Using a multi-source panel dataset of Chinese central SOEs from 2003 to 2023 and patent-based measures of exploratory and exploitative innovation, we find that higher administrative rank is primarily associated with greater exploratory innovation, alongside a negative relationship with exploitative innovation. Absorptive capacity reinforces the exploratory orientation associated with administrative rank, whereas deep internal hierarchies attenuate it. These findings suggest that administrative rank shapes innovation portfolios by structuring access to policy-backed resources, frontier knowledge, and strategically salient incentives. By highlighting differentiation within the central SOE sector, this study extends resource-based and incentive-based views of SOE innovation and shows how politically structured organizational position helps explain the allocation of effort between exploration and exploitation.

10.1016/j.technovation.2026.103712.a: This study examines the dimensional structure of Artificial Intelligence Anxiety among Brazilian creative professionals through a cross-cultural adaptation and validation of the Artificial Intelligence Anxiety Scale (AIAS). While the original four-factor structure of the scale—Learning, Job Replacement, AI Configuration, and Sociotechnical Blindness—is broadly replicated, findings from EFA and CFA revealed recurring patterns of greater empirical overlap between factors, lower compartmentalization among anxiety dimensions, and atypical psychometric behavior in specific items when compared to the original validation study. Furthermore, subgroup analyses demonstrate that learning-related anxiety is higher among younger professionals, suggesting that support needs may vary across career stages. These findings are consistent with the proposition that creative workers experience AI anxiety differently from the general-population samples originally used to validate the AIAS. Theoretically, these results extend the AIAS literature to a professional population whose identity is closely tied to authorship and originality, yet whose AI-related anxiety remains empirically understudied. Practically, the findings suggest that managerial responses centered exclusively on technical upskilling may be insufficient to address concerns — such as those tied to human-machine similarity and occupational replacement — that appear to co-occur among creative professionals.

10.1016/j.technovation.2026.103713.a: The transition toward sustainability in infrastructure sectors requires interventions that address systemic lock-ins rather than isolated technological improvements. However, innovation ecosystem research offers only limited guidance on how public-sector-driven ecosystems can be intentionally steered toward sustainability under conditions of structural inertia. This study employs Donella Meadows’ leverage points framework to identify and categorize potential systemic interventions in the Dutch road infrastructure innovation ecosystem. Using an action-oriented research design conducted over 1.5 years with public clients, contractors, and knowledge institutions, the study identifies 25 interventions across five thematic areas. The findings show that interventions predominantly target system design and feedback structures, the strengthening of governance, foresight, and integration capabilities rather than focusing on parameter-level change. This highlights how transformations in public-sector innovation ecosystems emerge through the gradual reconfiguration of rules, information flows, and coordination mechanisms. The study contributes to innovation ecosystem research by demonstrating how leverage points can be used to guide and structure ecosystem-level intervention strategies and support deliberate steering of public-sector-driven innovation ecosystems toward sustainability.

10.1016/j.technovation.2026.103716.a: Design capabilities have been recognized as drivers of innovation, yet the distinction between internal and external design integration remains largely underexplored, as do the ways through which these integration types contribute to new product development (NPD) performance. Drawing on the dynamic knowledge management view, this study conceptualizes internal and external design integration as distinct loci of market-facing knowledge generation that are associated with launch strategy proficiency and, in turn, with NPD performance. Survey data from 247 U.S. firms show an indirect association between both types of design integration and NPD performance through launch strategy proficiency. Market dynamism reveals a capability reversal. Under stable market conditions, internal design integration is positively associated with launch strategy proficiency, whereas external design integration becomes negatively associated with it at very low levels of dynamism. Under dynamic market conditions, external design integration is positively associated with launch strategy proficiency, whereas the association between internal design integration and launch strategy proficiency is attenuated. The findings connect the design and marketing research streams and offer guidance for decision-makers on aligning the locus of design integration with the level of market dynamism.

10.1016/j.technovation.2026.103717.a: Amid growing global uncertainty and supply chain disruptions, strengthening supply chain resilience has emerged as a key strategic priority for firms. Although artificial intelligence (AI) is revolutionising supply chain management, existing research lacks an understanding of the impacts of firm-level AI adoption on supply chain resilience, particularly through capability-building mechanisms. Drawing on knowledge-based dynamic capabilities theory and socio-technical systems theory, this paper constructs a theoretical framework to explain how firm-level AI adoption enhances supply chain resilience. Applying panel data from 3,252 Chinese A-share listed firms over the period 2010-2023, our findings reveal that AI adoption positively strengthens supply chain resilience. Mechanism analyses indicate that absorptive capability and innovative capability serve as significant mediators of this relationship, whereas adaptive capability does not. Moreover, top executives’ digital leadership positively moderates the AI adoption—supply chain resilience nexus. Further heterogeneity analysis shows that effects are relatively pronounced in non-state-owned enterprises, technology-intensive/non-manufacturing industries, and developed, highly marketized regions. These findings advance understanding of the mechanism whereby AI adoption fosters supply chain resilience through capability development and highlight digital leadership as a vital enabler in AI-driven digital transformation.

10.1016/j.technovation.2026.103718.a: This paper examines the evolution of urban industrial symbiosis (UIS) through a business ecosystem lens. UIS, defined as the synergistic integration of urban and industrial systems where waste and by-products are repurposed as industrial inputs, has demonstrated strong potential to address climate change, urbanization challenges, and supply chain vulnerabilities. Existing UIS research has primarily focused on material flows, network structures, and policy arrangements. However, limited attention has been paid to how coordination mechanisms evolve as ecosystem interdependence and complexity increase over time. This omission is consequential because even powerful coordinators face structural limits when coordinating expanding interdependencies among heterogeneous actors and resource flows, creating a coordination gap. Drawing on case studies of Ulsan (South Korea), Händelö (Sweden), EcoPark (Hong Kong), Metro Vancouver (Canada), Kalundborg (Denmark), HS Orka (Iceland), and Kawasaki (Japan), the paper develops a process model of UIS ecosystem coordination that links generation-processing-auxiliary (G-P-A) subsystems, coordination tensions and mechanisms, and governance pathways across three analytical phases. The study advances UIS research by shifting from exchange-oriented perspectives toward dynamic ecosystem coordination and theorizing how coordination mechanisms evolve under increasing ecosystem complexity. It further extends business ecosystem theory by explaining how increasingly distributed coordination capacity sustains ecosystem resilience as growing interdependence strains centralized orchestration.

10.1016/j.technovation.2026.103719.a: Design Science (DS) has attracted growing interest in entrepreneurship and innovation research in recent years. Typically implemented through projects, DS projects are often complex and challenging to manage. This study explores how DS projects can be effectively structured to support several tasks for DS project management particularly regarding the division of research tasks and the allocation of project resources. We present a framework that segments the content of DS projects into small, well-defined, and individually manageable research components. The framework enables researchers to assign resources strategically, assess the balance of research output, schedule and monitor activities systematically, and adapt to changes in scope and objectives during project execution. To illustrate the framework's practical utility, we draw on a case study involving the development of an innovative blockchain-based solution for VAT settlement in Denmark. Additionally, we evaluated the framework's general applicability by comparing it against ten DS projects described in the scientific literature. This is complemented with a discussion of how the framework can be embedded into the DS project management process according to established projects management standards. The evaluation results support our claims about the framework's broader applicability and its potential to improve DS project management.

10.1016/j.technovation.2026.103720.a: Drawing on Resource Orchestration Theory (ROT), this study examines whether data-driven decision-making (DDS) and adoption of Fintech innovations serves as serial mediation mechanisms linking IoT adoption and business model innovation (BMI). Moreover, it examines whether Artificial Intelligence (AI) capability significantly moderates the relationship between IoT adoption, DDS, and BMI. Using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) on data from 689 bank managers, we found that IoT adoption positive direct relationship with BMI, DDS, and Fintech innovation adoption. Moreover, DDS and Fintech innovation adoption positively affect BMI. DDS and Fintech innovation adoption mediated and serially mediated the relationship between IoT adoption and BMI. Finally, AI capability positively moderates between IoT adoption and BMI, and IoT adoption and DDS. This study advances digital innovation research by explaining how banks transform IoT adoption into business model innovation through data-driven decision-making, Fintech innovation adoption, and AI-enabled resource orchestration. The findings offer practical implications for banking leaders seeking to enhance their innovation capabilities through IoT-driven decision-making and AI-enabled resource management.

10.1016/j.technovation.2026.103721.a: This paper investigates the sources of invention novelty and their relationship to invention impact from an evolutionary perspective on knowledge recombination. Emphasizing the role of scientific knowledge in the inventive process, the study develops a refined analytical framework that categorizes sources of novelty into three types: scientific originality, technological originality, and recombinative creation. Analyzing 73,228 biotechnology patents granted by the USPTO between 2010 and 2021, along with their citations to scientific publications and patents, the study reveals that novelty — derived from original scientific knowledge, original technological knowledge, or recombinant approaches — has heterogeneous implications for invention impact. Specifically, scientific originality and recombinative creation are significantly associated with greater invention impact, whereas technological originality and dual originality in science and technology do not exhibit a significant effect. Furthermore, scientific originality increases invention impact by facilitating the integration of distant technological knowledge and previously disconnected knowledge components. These findings highlight the distinct roles of different novelty sources and elucidate the mechanisms through which new scientific knowledge influences invention impact, particularly in the context of science-intensive sectors.

10.1016/j.technovation.2026.103722.a: As universities play an increasingly central role in regional innovation, understanding how internal governance influences academic entrepreneurship is becoming essential. While prior research has emphasized external conditions for spin-off generation, this study shifts the focus inward, examining how board size and diversity are associated with the generation of university spin-offs. Further, this study addresses these effects with the consideration of vice-chancellor's professional characteristics. Based on the analysis of a panel dataset of UK universities through time-lagged models, the findings suggest that while board diversity consistently supports spin-off activity, the relationship between board size and spin-offs generation varies across institutional contexts. When adding the factors of leadership characteristics, the findings provide partially robust evidence that these characteristics may condition the effects of board governance: longer vice-chancellor's tenure may dampen entrepreneurial outcomes, whereas a science-based educational background appears to offer short-term advantages but may limit the benefits of board diversity, with the strength of this moderating effect varying across model specifications. This study adds to the literature on university governance and academic entrepreneurship showing how internal governance and leadership characteristics may condition the effectiveness of governance structures in academic spin-off generation.

10.1016/j.technovation.2026.103723.a: This study examines how digital transformation enables firms to maintain and strengthen innovation resilience amid geopolitical conflict. Based on the Knowledge Availability Constraint-Digital Dynamic Capability (KAC-DDC) framework, we treat dynamic directed inter-firm knowledge networks—constructed from patent citation links—as observable signals of corporate knowledge flows. Within these evolving networks, we develop a resilience metric, Knowledge Network Resilience (KNR), measuring corporate innovation resilience. Meanwhile, we employ the large language model ERNIE to develop a semantics-based measure of firms' digital transformation. The empirical analysis leverages sanction shocks associated with the 2018-2020 U.S.-China trade war, constructing firm-year samples within event windows centered on the year in which each industry first entered the sanctions list. The results show that, following sanction shocks, digital transformation partially offsets the adverse effect of technology sanctions on firms’ innovation resilience. Digital transformation also enhances the structural advantages of knowledge flow within knowledge networks, thereby amplifying resilience through knowledge-flow mechanisms. These effects are more pronounced in less munificent and less concentrated industries, and among firms with lower innovation-network embeddedness and more limited human capital.

10.1016/j.technovation.2026.103724.a: Patent abandonment can be conceived as a deliberate approach to orchestrate and streamline patent assets, which is often shaped by firms' innovation strategies. This study conceptualizes ambidextrous innovation leap as a strategic reconfiguration of innovation trajectories that redeploys and recombines existing knowledge resources across distinct innovation domains. It investigates how these leaps influence patent abandonment decisions. We propose that such transitions can either disrupt or reinforce the coherence of firms’ knowledge bases, thereby affecting the perceived value and retention of current patent holdings. We distinguish between two types of leaps: upward innovation leap, involving a shift from exploitative to exploratory innovation, and downward innovation leap, denoting the reverse transition. Using panel data on 1623 A-share listed firms in Shanghai and Shenzhen from 2003 to 2021, we find that upward innovation leap has a positive effect on patent abandonment, whilst downward innovation leap negatively affects patent abandonment. We also show that network centrality and knowledge integration capability both negatively moderate the relationship between ambidextrous innovation leaps and patent abandonment. By shedding light on these relationships, this study enriches the research on strategic antecedents of patent abandonment from a resource orchestration perspective, and also has important practical implications for firms making patent abandonment decisions during innovation transitions.

10.1016/j.technovation.2026.103725.a: Against the dual pressures of accelerated smart eldercare adoption and rising ethical risk, Generative AI (GenAI) is reshaping how value is created in elderly-care scenes. However, extant research has scarcely explored how GenAI—as an agent endowed with generative capabilities—deeply couples with eldercare scenes to reconfigure human-machine hybrid agency, thereby actualizing scene value co-creation. This study conducts an exploratory longitudinal dual-case analysis of iFlytek, an ecosystem orchestrator, and UBTECH, a vertical subordinate enterprise within China's smart eldercare sector. The findings reveal that: (1) Generative AI and eldercare scenes, serving as dual parallel elements, drive the emergence of hybrid agency. (2) Scene value co-creation evolves through three distinct stages: functional connection, precision service, and empathic symbiosis. Correspondingly, hybrid agency transitions from automated agency to augmented agency and ultimately to symbiotic agency, successively actualizing safety value exchange, value-in-use alignment, and embodied value symbiosis within respective scenes. (3) The ecosystem orchestrator adopts a centralized orchestration and cognitive connection path to construct a platform-based hybrid agency, while the subordinate enterprise employs the path of terminal embedding and embodied companionship to construct a vertical hybrid agency. (4) To mitigate the latent risks of value co-destruction during the evolutionary process, enterprises must establish dynamic governance mechanisms spanning from boundary constraints and human calibration to ethical correction. This research extends the theoretical boundaries of digital innovation within the context of an aging society and provides strategic insights for leveraging Tech for Good to address the global challenges of population aging.

10.1016/j.technovation.2026.103726.a: With an ageing population and fast development of AI, the labour force is drastically changing, which presents a need to understand how older adults experience and respond to technologically evolving work environments. Based on Possible Selves Theory, this research investigates how older adults understand the function of AI-enabled digital reskilling to inform future workforce possible selves and continued participation in employment in later life. Data were collected from 51 older adults via the Prolific Academic platform and were analysed using the Gioia methodology. Findings revealed that older adults view AI-enabled digital reskilling as a significant pathway to help them create their future workforce possible selves, which acts as an important motivation for continued participation in the workforce. Additionally, older adults evaluate their future working identities in terms of their expected ability, the likelihood of success, their skill sets, confidence, labour market opportunities, and age-related constraints. Thus, this study extends Possible Selves Theory by demonstrating how AI-enabled digital reskilling shapes future work identities and supports workforce adaptation in later life. The findings further suggest that organizations, policymakers, and digital platform designers should invest in accessible AI-enabled digital reskilling initiatives that foster workforce participation and promote inclusive ageing in the digital economy.

10.1016/j.technovation.2026.103727.a: This study examines the relationship between digital platform capability (DPC) and competitive advantage (CA) in platform companies, focusing on the mediating roles of intrapreneurship and user value co-creation. Using a two-wave, time-lagged survey of 236 platform firms, we tested our hypotheses with polynomial regression and response surface analysis. The results indicate that DPC, particularly integration and reconfiguration capabilities, is positively associated with CA. Moreover, both internal and external value co-creation factors, namely intrapreneurship and user value co-creation, significantly mediate this relationship. Our findings also suggest that CA is enhanced when intrapreneurship and user value co-creation are balanced, but declines when their development is uneven. These insights deepen our understanding of how platform companies can align internal and external value co-creation processes to leverage DPC for sustainable competitive advantage.

10.1016/j.technovation.2026.103728.a: The relationship between creativity and artificial intelligence (AI) has attracted widespread attention from the public, corporations, and academia. Advanced AI-based examples of artistic production, such as AI generated music, poetry, and paintings, have started transforming the creative and cultural industries. This study analyzed the componential model of creativity through the lens of the Generative AI (GenAI) artwork produced by artists. A qualitative approach was employed utilizing data collected from interviews with various artists, critics, and technicians who worked with GenAI, thereby helping in identifying the creativity paradoxes in the AI era. The results suggest that the use of GenAI has created dualities in the components of creativity, including tensions between extrinsic and intrinsic motivations, artistic and technical skills, and creations by an artist and those generated by AI. Given that AI will continue to develop, the cultural and creative industries need to find ways to navigate these creativity paradoxes.

10.1016/j.technovation.2026.103729.a: While product design is a key driver of organizational success, companies increasingly struggle to sustain relevance in markets with ever-shortening product lifecycles. This study investigates how products achieve longevity without frequent redesign. A historical analysis of the Toyota Crown Comfort taxi, which remained in production for approximately 23-years (1995–2018), is used as a case to examine institutional lock-in as a complementary explanation for design longevity. The results identify three interrelated institutional mechanisms operating at the government-, industry-, and consumer-levels that collectively reinforced the vehicle's enduring market position. Building on these findings, the study proposes a conceptual framework demonstrating how institutional ecosystems can sustain dominant product designs over time. The research contributes to the product design, timeless design, and institutional lock-in literatures by demonstrating that long-term institutional relationships may provide an alternative pathway to design longevity beyond continuous redesign and R&D investment.

10.1016/j.technovation.2026.103730.a: Artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping corporate strategy, yet how regional AI exposure (RAE), the intensity of local industry peers' AI inventive activities, shapes firms' data-driven value propositions (DDVPs) remains unclear. Using panel data on Chinese listed firms from 2013 to 2023, we examine the mechanism linking RAE to DDVPs. We find that higher RAE is associated with greater subsequent AI knowledge generation, which is more strongly related to efficiency-oriented than product-oriented DDVPs, reflecting an efficiency trap. Dynamic capabilities govern this conversion asymmetrically: sensing and seizing capabilities primarily strengthen efficiency-oriented DDVP, whereas reconfiguring capability is particularly important for elevating product-oriented DDVP. These findings extend DDVP research beyond firm internal explanations by incorporating regional AI environments and show how distinct dynamic capability dimensions shape heterogeneous value-creation orientations.

10.1016/j.technovation.2026.103731.a: This study examines how organizations pursue technological sovereignty while embedded in infrastructures controlled by geopolitical competitors. We address this question through an in-depth longitudinal case study of Mistral AI (2023–2025), Europe's only frontier-scale Large Language Model developer competing with American incumbents. Our analysis draws on two primary data sources collected over the firm's first three years: 16 media interviews with CEO Arthur Mensch and 30 monthly activity reports published by Mistral, triangulated with technical documentation, industry analyses, and European policy documents. We employed an abductive analytical approach, combining iterative open and focused coding of institutional work practices with theoretical dimensioning and process tracing across four temporal phases of the company's evolution. Our findings reveal three interrelated forms of institutional work: selective decoupling of critical dependencies while maintaining beneficial connections, strategic leveraging of embeddedness in some structures to contest dominance in others, and structural reconfiguration creating alternative institutional arrangements. These practices constitute geopolitical embedded agency, a distinctive form of organizational action characterized by material rather than symbolic embeddedness; cross-scalar institutional contradictions; and sovereignty objectives that reshape conventional organizational rationality. Our framework contributes to institutional work theory and emerging technology sovereignty scholarship while extending analytically to other capital-intensive sectors facing geopolitical dependencies.

10.1016/j.technovation.2026.103732.a: Innovation propensity (IP) is an important antecedent of firms' innovation activities and innovation outputs. This study develops and validates an approach to measuring corporate innovation propensity using annual report texts, and further examines its predictive role in subsequent innovation behavior and its economic effects. Based on a sample of Chinese A-share high-tech listed firms from 2007 to 2020, this study employs a BERT–BiLSTM–CRF model to identify product and technology terms from the Management Discussion and Analysis (MD&A) sections of annual reports, and constructs a firm-level measure of innovation propensity accordingly. The results show that innovation propensity can predict firms' R&D investment and knowledge accumulation, while also significantly improving firm performance. Further analysis indicates that innovation propensity also affects firms’ capital market outcomes. This study advances the identification and measurement of innovation propensity from a text-analytics perspective, deepens the understanding of the antecedents of corporate innovation from the perspectives of knowledge management and dynamic capabilities, and provides new empirical evidence for revealing the economic consequences of managerial innovation propensity.

10.1016/j.technovation.2026.103733.a: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly positioned as a means of advancing the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), yet its contribution remains conditional, uneven, and context-dependent. To explain this variation, we organize the evidence through a single integrative lens: the AI-SDGs value cycle. The cycle comprises five interdependent functions - mapping opportunities, mobilizing capabilities, deploying applications, governing legitimacy and accountability, and evaluating sustainable value creation and destruction. It connects evidence across technologies, teams, organizations, sectors, cities, markets, and public institutions without reducing diverse contributions to a catalog of applications. The synthesis shows that sustainable outcomes arise not from technological capability alone, but from its combination with organizational readiness, sectoral fit, responsible governance, stakeholder representation, and attention to cross-goal and lifecycle consequences. Collectively, the papers move research beyond broad claims about AI's potential toward explanations of when, how, for whom, and at what cost AI supports sustainable development. They establish governance as constitutive of sustainable innovation and reveal value creation and destruction as simultaneous possibilities rather than separable outcomes. Drawing these insights together, this editorial synthesizes the 17 accepted articles in the Technovation Special Issue “Artificial Intelligence for the Sustainable Development Goals” and clarifies their collective contribution. It concludes with a focused research agenda organized around the same value cycle and directed toward cumulative, comparative, and impact-oriented inquiry.

10.1016/j.technovation.2026.103734.a: Mission-oriented innovation policy (MOIP) has emerged as a prominent approach for addressing grand societal challenges by directing innovation toward clearly defined public missions. Although prior research has advanced understanding of mission design, policy coordination, and ecosystem governance, limited attention has been paid to how mission-oriented policies are translated into organizational practices. Addressing this gap, this study develops and empirically tests a policy-to-practice translation framework that explains how policy directionality becomes embedded within organizations through responsible innovation (RI) governance and subsequently influences employee behavioral outcomes. Drawing on the literatures on RI, organizational governance, and trust, RI is conceptualized as an organizational governance mechanism that translates external policy expectations into structured innovation practices. Innovation trust functions as the behavioral mechanism linking RI governance to sustainability-oriented behavioral intentions, while organizational ESG capability and individual Anthropocene awareness serve as important boundary conditions. The proposed framework is examined using a theory-testing dominant mixed-method design combining hierarchical linear modeling, structural equation modeling, and comparative qualitative case studies. Survey data from 538 employees across 38 Korean firms are complemented by qualitative evidence from mission-priority industries. The findings indicate that perceived organizational alignment with mission-oriented policy directionality is associated with employee behavioral intentions through RI governance and innovation trust. This study advances mission-oriented innovation research by introducing a policy-to-practice translation perspective and offers practical implications for governments and organizations implementing mission-oriented innovation policies.

10.1016/j.technovation.2026.103735.a: Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming the theory and practice of innovation and marketing, yet its deployment at their intersection remains only partially understood. Existing literature has not thoroughly examined which AI capabilities (analytical, generative) are more appropriate during different stages of the new product development (NPD) process, how a core marketing factor, customer involvement, conditions the outcomes of these capabilities, or how AI-related risks and governance mechanisms shape NPD performance across stages. This study addresses these gaps by proposing a novel conceptual framework that links the two distinct AI capability types to specific NPD stages, examines how customer involvement moderates the relationship between AI capabilities and NPD outcomes, integrates AI hallucination risk as a formal boundary condition differentiating the failure modes of AI capabilities across stages, and extends the framework to NPD governance mechanisms including gate evaluations, feedback loops, and cross-functional coordination. The paper contributes to research and practice by (1) offering a set of propositions regarding AI’s role at the intersection of innovation and marketing, (2) providing theoretically derived guidance for managers on deploying AI capabilities during NPD while recognizing the marketing imperative of customer involvement, and (3) outlining a future research agenda on AI-enabled innovation which is of crucial importance for the future of business. Collectively, the paper advances a more theoretically rigorous and practically relevant understanding of AI’s transformative role in innovation and marketing.

10.1016/j.technovation.2026.103736.a: A firm's research portfolio often faces a tension between reliance on dominant technologies and the pursuit of technological differentiation. This study examines how invention teams generate such differentiation by linking network structure to innovation outcomes. We develop a novel semantic distance measure based on patent text, capturing technological differentiation along a continuous space rather than discrete classification categories. Using this measure, we show that invention teams achieve higher levels of differentiation when they combine strong internal cohesion with diverse external network connections. Specifically, cohesive internal ties facilitate knowledge integration, while external ties spanning structural holes expand access to novel knowledge. These findings highlight the importance of balancing cohesion and brokerage in shaping technological differentiation and offer new insights into the organization of inventive activity.

10.1016/j.technovation.2026.103737.a: In increasingly volatile markets, firms are turning to artificial intelligence (AI) to enhance innovation and maintain a competitive edge. However, many organizations continue to struggle to translate AI investments into meaningful innovation outcomes. This study develops and empirically tests a framework examining how AI capability is transformed into business-to-business (B2B) marketing innovation through organizational agility and product innovation intensity. Drawing on survey data from 239 Chinese firms, the findings reveal that AI capability drives B2B marketing innovation through a theorized sequential relationship, in which organizational agility enables intensified product innovation, which in turn supports market-facing innovation. Furthermore, market turbulence acts as a contingent boundary condition, amplifying the effects of AI capability on product innovation intensity and downstream innovation outcomes, while not significantly affecting its relationship with organizational agility. By conceptualizing AI capability as an enabling capability architecture that activates sensing, seizing, and reconfiguring processes, this research advances dynamic capability theory and provides a more granular explanation of how AI is translated into innovation. It also distinguishes between innovation generation (product innovation intensity) and innovation realization (B2B marketing innovation), offering a process-based account of capability-to-innovation transformation. The study provides actionable insights for managers on developing integrated AI capability, enhancing organizational agility, and strategically intensifying innovation efforts under varying levels of market turbulence.

10.1016/j.technovation.2026.103738.a: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is disrupting creative work and challenging occupational identities, yet limited research has examined how creators experience and respond to these changes. Drawing on Albert Ellis’s ABC model, this study investigates relationships among GenAI adoption, identity threat, job crafting, and identity consequences. Using a two-stage exploratory mixed-method design with digital content creators in China, we combined BERTopic analysis of 2994 open-ended responses with structural equation modelling of matched survey data from 1698 creators. The findings show that GenAI is widely perceived through coexisting beliefs about threat, opportunity, and the unknown, and that these beliefs give rise to differentiated job crafting behaviours, including approach crafting, avoidance crafting, and identity crafting. Notably, identity crafting plays an important role in fostering a responsible creative identity and self-actualization. This study advances theorizing on AI technological innovation and creative labour by showing how job crafting translates GenAI disruption into responsibility-oriented and meaning-centered identity reshaping. It also offers actionable insights for creators, platforms, and creative communities seeking to support collaborative, sustainable, and ethically grounded human–AI co-creation.

10.1016/j.technovation.2026.103739.a: The convergence of digital and green technologies (DGT) is emerging as a key driver of low-carbon transformation, yet its effects on eco-innovation remain understudied. Using matched micro-enterprise data and highly granular patent data from 2010 to 2023, we employ co-classification analysis to identify firm-level DGT convergence behaviors. Our findings reveal that DGT convergence significantly improves both the quantity and quality of firm eco-innovation by strengthening technology absorption capacity, expanding knowledge breadth, and facilitating technological spillovers. Furthermore, stricter intellectual property protection amplifies this positive effect. The analysis further shows that DGT convergence achieves its greatest impact through AI-green integration, while also being pivotal for advancing energy-saving/emission-reduction technologies and for diversifying and specializing the eco-innovation portfolio. Our study, from a technological convergence perspective, provides managerial implications for fostering digital-green convergence in eco-innovation.

10.1016/j.technovation.2026.103740.a: This study examines how governance in business-NGO collaborations conditions co-creation for sustainable innovation under institutional plurality. Drawing on institutional logics theory, we conduct a qualitative cross-case study of five Scandinavian retail firms and their NGO partners. We identify three recurrent governance configurations: separated coexistence, assimilated coexistence, and logic blending. The configurations differ in how partners manage organizational boundaries, allocate decision authority, integrate knowledge, and establish accountability. In the cases studied, separated coexistence was recurrently associated with regulative innovation, where protected organizational distance supported credible monitoring and verification. Assimilated coexistence was recurrently associated with inclusive sustainable business innovation, where NGO knowledge entered bounded parts of firm-led innovation. Logic blending was most evident in social impact innovation, where joint problem framing, shared interpretation of evidence, and relational accountability supported long-term societal outcomes. These relationships represent empirical tendencies rather than necessary, sufficient, or exclusive associations. Different configurations may coexist across activities and may evolve as collaborations mature. The study extends institutional logics research by showing how responses to plurality are operationalized as interorganizational governance arrangements that structure decision rights, knowledge interfaces, boundaries, and accountability. It contributes to sustainable co-creation research by explaining why different innovation tasks call for different combinations of governance practices.

10.1016/j.technovation.2026.103741.a: This study demonstrates that the relationship between the breadth of engagement with innovation ecosystem actors across four geographical dimensions shapes innovation outcomes and is subject to firms’ perceptions of risk and uncertainty. Using firm-level data for 14,382 innovative firms and 28,913 firm-year observations from 2004 to 2016 in the United Kingdom (UK), we find a strong link between the breadth of engagement with innovation ecosystem actors regionally, nationally, and internationally and the commercialization of innovation. Economic risk and market uncertainty condition the collaboration–innovation relationship, but the robustness of these effects show that geographical location of partners matters. Identifying this idiosyncratic relationship contributes to the open innovation and innovation ecosystems literature by demonstrating that changes in knowledge collaboration with ecosystem actors increase innovation and that uncertainty and risk act as boundary conditions for innovation.

10.1016/j.technovation.2026.103742.a: This study examines the growth hacking mechanism and its antecedents in enhancing Small and Medium-sized Enterprises (SME) entrepreneurial performance in developing economies. Despite growing interest in growth hacking, prior studies remain limited in providing a comprehensive theoretical explanation and empirical validation, particularly within the context of developing countries. Using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling, this study analyzes data from 318 SMEs that have adopted digitalization practices. Drawing on the Technology–Organization–Environment (TOE) framework, it examines technological factors (big data analytics and digital transformation), organizational factors (entrepreneurial leadership and learning ambidexterity), and environmental factors (government support and university partnership). The findings indicate that big data analytics, digital transformation, entrepreneurial leadership, and learning ambidexterity significantly enhance growth hacking effectiveness. Government support emerges as a key external enabler, while university partnership shows no significant effect. This study contributes to the literature by positioning growth hacking as a cross-functional capability within the TOE framework and highlighting the contextual importance of institutional support in developing economies.

10.1016/j.technovation.2026.103743.a: Energy Communities (ECs) are increasingly recognized as collaborative ecosystems that support energy transition. However, existing research has predominantly explained their emergence from macro- and meso-level perspectives, offering limited insight into micro-level mechanisms. Although broader ecosystem research has only recently begun to explain ecosystem-level outcomes from a micro-level perspective, treating individuals as the primary unit of analysis, it has paid limited attention to the relational mechanisms through which individual actions and interactions contribute to ecosystem emergence. To address this gap, this study adopts a microfoundational perspective to examine the creation and development of an energy community ecosystem through an in-depth qualitative case study conducted in Southern Italy. Drawing on semi-structured interviews triangulated with multiple documentary sources analyzed through Reflexive Thematic Analysis, the findings identify three relational microfoundational mechanisms, namely micro-level collaborative initiatives, micro-relational engagement toward cultural change, and relation-driven energy inclusion that explain how energy community ecosystems progressively emerge from individual actions and interactions across the ideation, formalization, and growth phases. The study advances the explanatory capacity of the microfoundational perspective by extending its application to energy community ecosystems, providing actionable insights for designing inclusive, context-sensitive interventions tailored to different phases of ecosystem development.

10.1016/j.technovation.2026.103744.a: Business Models (BMs) are central to how SMEs compete in dynamic environments. Despite their importance, research on BMs in SMEs remains fragmented, with limited integration across theoretical perspectives and empirical insights. This study addresses that gap through a systematic literature review of 405 articles retrieved from Scopus and WoS, mapping the intellectual structure of BMs research in SMEs. Using bibliometric and thematic analysis, six dominant research clusters are identified and synthesised. Drawing on key theories, including the resource-based view, dynamic capabilities, and stakeholder theory, the study develops an integrative framework linking contextual determinants, configuration mechanisms, and the strategic, operational, and societal outcomes of BMs in SMEs. The framework positions BMs in SMEs as context-sensitive systems shaped by the interplay of resources, adaptive capabilities, and stakeholder expectations. The paper concludes with a future research agenda that highlights overlooked areas, including how SMEs navigate overlapping pressures, internal heterogeneity, micro-level BM processes, responsible digital practices, and diverse network structures. By integrating fragmented insights into a coherent framework, this review provides a foundation for advancing theory and offering practical guidance for SMEs operating under resource constraints and environmental turbulence.

10.1016/j.technovation.2026.103745.a: Silver tourism is a rapidly growing segment of global tourism, yet older adults face persistent digital divides when engaging with smart travel platforms. This study examines technology use intentions among 800 silver tourists in Greece (Athens) and the UK (Birmingham) through a complexity-informed bounded Rational Choice Theory framework. Integrating fuzzy-set Qualitative Comparative Analysis (fsQCA) with Necessary Condition Analysis (NCA), the study identifies sufficient configurations of six conditions namely perceived usefulness, ease of use, subjective norms, cognition, trust, and perceived competence alongside city-specific necessary conditions. Subjective norms emerge as necessary in Athens (collectivist, digitally uneven), while trust and perceived competence are necessary in Birmingham (individualist, digitally mature). In total, the analysis identified three acceptable pathways: one shared pathway, the Cognitive-Competence users which was valid in both Greek and British contexts, and two context-specific pathways, namely the Usage-Norm Consumers in Greece and the Cognitive Trust-in-Competence users in the UK. Post-evaluation interviews with six tourism managers confirmed the ecological validity of the identified pathways and strengthened the practical relevance of the findings. Findings extend digital divide theory, Rational Choice Theory, and complexity theory, offering culturally tailored guidance for inclusive tourism technology design.

10.1016/s0166-4972(00)00002-x.a: The overall intent of this research was to explore possible ways of project success, so as to incorporate two important features, such as service quality in construction delivered by contractors and the project owners expectations. Special consideration has been given to service gap analysis as a diagnostic tool on the differences and similarities of the views of project owners and contractors concerning 15 attributes. This technique highlights and confirms some construction problems and their nature sought by means of a structured questionnaire survey completed by 138 participants. This study built up a body of information on project construction characteristics in present conditions, tested the assumptions among the project team and raised important issues relating to the debates surrounding it. We find that there was an almost complete lack of attention devoted to owners satisfaction which undoubtedly contributed to poor performance. Current construction practices and technical failures are minute compared with client enormous dissatisfactions. Findings partially support our contentions that trust is an important role for cooperative endeavours. Therefore, project owners and contractors should re-evaluate their mode of operation and plan for adjustment which requires time and dedication on both sides. It is also concluded that the propositions suggested by the framework and the implications discussed can lead to more informed discussion of some of the controversial issues that face the construction at this time. These results suggest that the insights provided should be taken seriously and provide a basis for thinking about the implications for future development of the construction industry as a whole and for future research.

10.1016/s0166-4972(00)00003-1.a: The study examines the feasibility of producing charcoal from wood wastes. The technical study was highlighted and the financial viability was analyzed. The socio-economic and marketing studies were pointed out. In this attempt, primary data were collected from logging operators and helpers, the charcoal vendors, and the suppliers of construction materials in Ife Central and Ife South local governments of Osun State using unstructured personal interview. The technical data were collected from documented records. The financial analysis was done through the use of cost-benefit ratio and production cost analysis. The data were projected for 5 years using the arithmetical straight line method. The results show that the fabricated masonry block kiln could yield a profitability efficiency of 31% in the first year of operation and 37.2% in the fifth year. The cost benefit ratios of 1.44 (1st year), 1.59 (3rd year), and 1.60 (5th year) positively indicate the profitability of the industry. The results therefore suggest that utilization of wood residuals is a strategy in harnessing rural resources and it would also considerably boost the profitability of rural resources.

10.1016/s0166-4972(00)00004-3.a: The development of an innovative trend analysis of the library and information science is discussed. This revealed that the library world is in the process of technological restructuring. The methods and best practices and the combination of library functions are also discussed in detail.

10.1016/s0166-4972(00)00006-7.a: This paper reports on recent research aimed at improving interaction between the Foresight programme and SMEs (Small and Medium sized Enterprises). The UK Foresight programme is a major input into the ongoing debate into innovation and the science base in the United Kingdom. SMEs have so far failed in significant numbers to become involved in the forward thinking culture that Foresight promotes. This paper examines the problem of how Foresight can be packaged to make it more SME-friendly. This work used the context of knowledge transfer and the intermediary role of the business support community. Conceptual frameworks were developed to describe SMEs' managerial attitudes to the future and to give structure to the business support community. Fieldwork revealed patterns of interaction between SMEs and business support intermediaries. A model was developed showing a system for targeting Foresight to SMEs through the engagement of these intermediaries. This paper examines the implications of this model and locates the contributions of the research.

10.1016/s0166-4972(00)00007-9.a: This article records the findings from the survey about the pattern of current uses and future tendency of Advanced Manufacturing Technologies (AMT). The empirical data come from the project International Manufacturing Strategy Survey (IMSS) which covers 18 countries. It was found that CAD, MRP, LAN, and CNC machines are the most popular AMTs used now. It seems that there is a sequence of adopting AMT, namely from simple to complicated. Green field and fully-integrated CIM systems seem to be rare. In three years, the uses of CAPP and shared database will significantly increase, which indicate the increase in integration level of manufacturing system. However, the main configuration of manufacturing will be stand-alone, islands of automation, and limited integration. Fully computerised integration in manufacturing system will unlikely be the main model in the near future. Regarding the relationship between AMT uses and performance improvement seems to be complicated and a couple of different patterns are identified. Practical implications, limitations and future research are also discussed finally.

10.1016/s0166-4972(00)00008-0.a: This paper discusses the process of technological flows between countries. In particular, we discuss how technology can flow from the originating country to a foreign country, and how in turn direct foreign investment by the recipient foreign country can return technological advances to the originating country. We apply our discussion to the automobile industry in the US, and present evidence that direct investment by Japanese auto firms, and in particular the pioneering involvement in the US of Honda, has improved the rate of technological advance by US manufacturers.

10.1016/s0166-4972(00)00009-2.a: The paper investigates the technological spill-over effects from the Volvo Aero Corporation. Experiences and technological know-how from the military engine sector have been a prerequisite for development of other commerical business within Volvo Aero. With regard to the Swedish competitiveness clusters development of new business areas and spill-overs have moved from the defence cluster into traditional Swedish clusters. The company has extensive research networks, but the extent and nature of technology spill-over within these external networks are yet unknown.

10.1016/s0166-4972(00)00011-0.a: This paper analyzes the main results of a survey to 28 automotive suppliers in the Spanish region of Aragon. It has been found in a regression analysis that the rotation of tasks and teamworking are positively correlated with the training and the use of modular components. Nearly half of the companies cooperate with customers, suppliers, and technological centers to improve their production processes but only two companies cooperate with their customers in component development and design which indicates an underinvolvement of the surveyed companies with the automotive manufacturers. The companies are much more integrated with the automakers in the delivery process, since more than half of the companies have daily deliveries and directly to the assembly line of the automaker.

10.1016/s0166-4972(00)00012-2.a: This research paper evolves from problems related to the environment as the result of today's product-based society and especially the end-of-life management of cars. The purpose is to identify key elements in car-scrapping approaches with the potential to meet the following three goals: containing the environmental damage from end-of-life cars, improvement of current end-of-life car management from an environmental and resource utilization standpoint, and fostering manufacturing of scrap-adapted/recycled cars. An attempt is made to analyze how financial resources could be organized for the ELV recycling system. A few suggestions have been made in order to foster attainment of the above-mentioned goals through an extended producer responsibility through requisite market oriented financial support. In short, this paper takes a look at the economic feasibility and ingredients for success of a market for recyclables. It lays emphasis on some kind of transparency at the economic and technical levels.

10.1016/s0166-4972(00)00013-4.a: The importance of information technology (IT) in the modern day business transaction cannot be over-emphasized. The impact assessment of the technology on any business is expedient so as to objectively determine its influence on a specific aspect of the organization. This study therefore assessed the organizational impact of IT on some banks and insurance firms in Nigeria. Eight leading commercial banks and six highly rated insurance firms which have branches in Lagos, the commercial nerve centre of Nigeria, and two other important state capitals, were selected for this study. Data were obtained from both the customers and workers at the banks and insurance firms. The data were analyzed using percentage and five-point Likert scale to objectively determine the local and global impacts of IT on the banks and insurance firms. The local impact criteria considered are: time savings, error rate reduction, enhanced management decision making, and improved service delivery. On the 5-point likert scale, there was positive impact on IT on the local criteria in the mean range of 1-3 at Lagos and Ibadan with Osogbo having a mean in the range of 3-5 which indicates otherwise. Also, the calculated mean of the IT impact on global criteria such as competitive advantage, high revenue generation, market segmentation and forecasting are in the range of 1-3 for all sampled cites. The study also revealed that there was positive impact of IT on both the induced local and global criteria. The induced local impact criteria identified are competitive advantage, market segmentation, high revenue generation, and forecasting while development of business niche, increased market share and network insecurity constituted the induced global impact criteria.

10.1016/s0166-4972(00)00014-6.a: This paper analyses the `importance' and `awareness' of a set of established `external communication' determinants of technological innovation in the context of a newly industrialized country. The researcher interviewed 105 Greek manufacturing companies, measuring their innovation rate as well as 23 potential `external communication' determinants. Using correlation and regression analyses, the initial group of 23 factors was reduced to a subset of 10 `major importance' determinants of innovation. The results supported two hypotheses related with newly industrialized countries, namely: 1. searching for product-specific information is more important for innovation than scanning more general market and technological information; and 2. the co-operation with partnering organizations is more important for innovation than the co-operation with assisting organizations. The `objective' results were then compared with the `perceptions' of the managers on the important factors determining innovation (also measured during the interviews). Overall, the perceptual analysis confirmed the significance of the subset of statistically important variables. Therefore, the hypothesis that in newly industrialized countries the managers are generally unaware of the important determinants of innovation was rejected. Generally, the study provided supporting evidence to the `contingency' school of thought, suggesting that there are no universally applicable recipes for successful innovation management.

10.1016/s0166-4972(00)00015-8.a: Assisted technology transfer (ATT) actions towards small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) have been growing in recent years, as governments of industrialized countries have acknowledged the importance of SMEs in industrial economic systems. In spite of their success, SMEs show several weaknesses in technological development. This introduces opportunities for public intervention aimed at sustaining technological development in SMEs, especially through technology transfer processes. Although the need for this kind of action is widely accepted, how to implement ATT is still unclear, as regards both the choice of potential beneficiaries and the actual implementation of the transfer process. This paper presents a project of ATT sponsored by the Science Park of Liguria and addressed to 30 small firms in the sectors of plant engineering and industrial automation. After reviewing the rationale for ATT actions and highlighting some crucial questions related to its implementation, it gives an extensive picture of the approach adopted. Finally, it attempts to rationalize the case, in order to highlight problems and offer possible solutions.

10.1016/s0166-4972(00)00016-x.a: This paper examines similarities and differences between small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) with different levels of reported product innovation. These SMEs are located in an area (the Niagara region in southern Ontario) that has suffered industrial decline during the last three decades. Furthermore, SMEs in this region are in traditional or late-cycle manufacturing sectors (e.g., fabricated metal). The research findings show that SMEs claiming to pursue product innovation are better performers in terms of total and export sales. SMEs with higher levels of product innovation rated the following strategies as significantly more important compared with SMEs with lower levels of innovation: the expansion of R&D efforts, incremental innovation, new product development, and new export market development. In contrast, SMEs with lower levels of product innovation emphasized the importance of cost-based pricing and their market development is focused on Canada. Both groups of product innovators have adopted similar types of process innovation, but the SMEs with higher levels of product innovation note higher levels of benefit from process changes compared with manufacturers with lower levels of product innovators. In a similar fashion, SMEs with higher levels of product innovation use external service inputs for problem-solving and business development in the face of a multitude of competitive problems within the local economy (such as the lack of skilled or specialist labor, tax burden, etc). In sum, SMEs pursuing innovation in traditional sectors in peripheral regions are showing better possibilities of adjustment in a dynamic global environment.

10.1016/s0166-4972(00)00017-1.a: This paper analyses the use of the Internet in recruitment processes using a new model for decomposing e-commerce. It presents two case studies from central Scotland: one, Cadence, is a significant knowledge-based inward investor; the other, Melville Craig, the premier staffing agency in Scotland. A methodology and model for e-commerce are outlined and used to analyze the Internet offers of searchers, finders and intermediaries in recruitment processes, The paper argues that the use of the Internet in recruitment processes is likely to generalize, alter the interface between some internal and external labour markets and adjust present patterns of intermediation in labour markets. It is further suggested that the conceptions behind current research programmes in labour market theory may require re-thinking in the light of the use of the Internet. The paper concludes by highlight a range of public policy issues.

10.1016/s0166-4972(00)00018-3.a: The introduction and development of innovation in small and medium-sized firms has most often been considered as being driven by the entrepreneur-owner who is supposed to conceive the innovation and then consistently sponsor and pursue its implementation within the organization. However, when the innovation turns from an abstract idea into a change embedded within a social network, fear of modifying the power map within the network can lead to inconsistent behaviors on the part of the owner, who may even try to make the innovation process fail. An ethnographic study was carried out in a small Italian firm that manufactures staircases, observing from start to finish the process by which a new Information System was implemented. From the field notes, clear pro- and anti-innovation coalitions emerged. The findings of the study noted that the entrepreneur-owner, although unanimously acknowledged to have argued in favor of the innovation, withdrew his support from its implementation when he realized that, contrary to his expectations, it increased the power of a few core actors defined, in this instance, as those actors with greater and more sought-after technical know-how and skills.

10.1016/s0166-4972(00)00019-5.a: Advanced ceramics and processes have potential applications in many fields. This ranges from heat engines to communication and energy transmission. The evolution of ceramic technology is discussed. An advanced ceramic tree is developed to illustrate the potential application areas.

10.1016/s0166-4972(00)00020-1.a: The introduction of any new technology may need new institutional structures, but it definitely involves establishment of linkages among various actors, agencies and institutions. The concept of `National System of Innovation' captures the process of networking and has been found to be useful for analyzing knowledge intensive technology sectors, such as biotechnology. This paper presents the results of an attempt made to analyze the Indian System of Innovation in Biotechnology by taking up a case study of commercialization of plant tissue culture technology in the case of cardamom. The aspects examined include generation of knowledge, process of learning, the institutional arrangement, networking among various institutions and the role of the government. The paper reflects the importance of each type of actor and the government support at research and all the more at production and diffusion levels. It brings out the reasons which necessitated adoption of the new technology (plant tissue culture) in the case of cardamom and the success achieved in its commercialization.

10.1016/s0166-4972(00)00022-5.a: Since 1975, India has built 25 satellites under the satellite programme.
